title: MCP tooling gaps for the new Kubernetes deployment
summary: The existing MCP surface (23 tools in orchestrator/mcp_tools.py) is pipeline-centric — it assumes the orchestrator and gateway are already up and talking to each other. That assumption is exactly what breaks first on a fresh k3s-native deployment, which is why the #1692 validation session fell back to raw kubectl for every debug iteration. This analysis recommends the refiner's Option A (ship the umbrella in #1759): five new MCP tools (validate_deployment_manifests, validate_network_isolation, prune_stale_worktrees, get_deployment_context, rebuild_and_rollout) plus two new skills (deployment-diagnose, agent-diagnose). rebuild_and_rollout is in scope now that #1763 (SHA-tagged local images) has merged (Decision 4 resolution); the submit_task task-id-reuse papercut is deferred to #1804 (Decision 3); skills ship against currently reachable evidence without waiting on log persistence, with log-persistence tracked in #1805 (Decision 5); and the in-situ gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL misconfig is filed as a separate issue. All five tools land as new entries in orchestrator/mcp_tools.py PIPELINE_TOOLS + _handle_* methods on PipelineToolHandler (schema at line 64+, class at line 690) that proxy to new orchestrator HTTP routes; the two skills land as SKILL.md files under skills/ alongside the existing sdlc/babysit-pr/egg-setup skills. Both skills explicitly reference #1806 (overseer-overlap investigation, non-blocking) so the known-failure catalogue and the existing overseer do not diverge. k8s-cluster work reuses the existing get_kubernetes_client() singleton (kubernetes_client.py:943) and _resolve_job_name helper (line 867) — no new auth surface, no new architecture.
revision_notes: Revision 2 addresses reviewer_plan NACK (timestamp 2026-04-21T21:11:13). Blocking fixes: (1) added tool_5_rebuild_and_rollout per D4 resolution (#1763 merged); (2) moved Q-3/Q-4/Q-5/Q-6/Q-7 from open_questions to a new resolved_inputs section citing decision-8 verbatim, keeping only Q-1 (default overlay path) and Q-2 (egg-agents vs egg-probes namespace) as legitimately open. Non-blocking improvements: (a) tool_2 validate_network_isolation now explicitly checks CNI enforcement via get_deployment_context before running the probe and specifies concrete probe Job labels (app.kubernetes.io/component: agent + egg.probe: true, per risk_analyst RISK-1); (b) tool_1 validate_deployment_manifests now states runtime gating explicitly per RISK-5 so k3s-specific heuristics do not fire on a different k8s flavor; (c) tool_3 prune_stale_worktrees text reconciled with affected_files.gateway: tool is orchestrator-owned, worktree mutex is in gateway, MCP tool proxies to new gateway endpoint; (d) skill_2 agent-diagnose composed-primitives corrected — removed get_consensus_status/send_message as the synthetic egress probe (those are pipeline-state tools, not network probes); egress now reuses validate_network_isolation's probe path; (e) skill_2 catalogue now enumerates the five identifier-translation asymmetries from Q2 resolution; (f) both skills reference #1806 so implementation avoids overseer overlap; (g) mcp_rate_limit_consideration now explicitly addresses skill-level recursion risk.

problem_statement.description: Validating #1692 (Docker → k3s migration) on a fresh machine surfaced a long list of deployment bugs that the current MCP tooling gave no help diagnosing. Every iteration fell back to raw `kubectl get pods`, `kubectl describe pod`, `kubectl logs deploy/…`, and `docker build … && sudo k3s ctr images import -`. The same failure classes recurred six times during the validation pass (#1760, #1764, #1765, #1766, #1767, #1768, #1769) and cluster into two shapes: identifier-translation asymmetries (Pod UID vs Job UID) and role/auth boundary errors. The issue proposes closing these blind spots by adding deterministic MCP tools for deployment-level actions/fetches and skills that compose them with judgment to narrate findings.
goals: Add five MCP tools: validate_deployment_manifests, validate_network_isolation, prune_stale_worktrees, get_deployment_context, rebuild_and_rollout. All live in the orchestrator's in-process MCP server and proxy to new orchestrator HTTP routes following the established 23-tool pattern.

Add two operator-side skills: deployment-diagnose (walks pod describe → Events → image-vs-manifest diff → resolved mounts → health body → applied-vs-running spec diff → gateway silent-failure scan) and agent-diagnose (Job spec → pod statuses → last 100 log lines → Events → resolved env → synthetic egress probe via validate_network_isolation → pattern-matched error classification covering the five identifier-translation asymmetries from decision-8 Q2).

Reuse existing primitives everywhere: get_kubernetes_client() singleton for cluster access, _resolve_job_name() for Pod-UID↔Job-name translation, list_containers + get_container_logs MCP tools composed by skills, WORKTREE_BASE_DIR + cleanup_orphaned_worktrees for prune_stale_worktrees, egg_prompt / SKILL.md frontmatter pattern for new skills.

Preserve dual-runtime compatibility: get_deployment_context is multi-runtime by design; the other four new tools are k8s-specific and must return a structured 'not applicable on EGG_RUNTIME=docker' error rather than crashing. k3s-specific heuristics inside tools MUST be gated on get_deployment_context reporting a k3s runtime (risk_analyst RISK-5).

Both skills explicitly reference #1806 (overseer-overlap investigation) so the known-failure catalogue is built in awareness of, not in isolation from, the existing overseer agent's anomaly-detection surface (risk_analyst RISK-11).

Acceptance criterion is end-to-end: a re-run of the #1692 validation session using only the new tools/skills should not need to fall back to raw kubectl (or raw `make redeploy`) for any of the failure modes documented in the issue (#1760, #1764, #1766, #1767, #1768, #1769).
non_goals: submit_task 'silently reuses an existing task_id' papercut fix (decision-8 Q5: surfaced as a known concern; actual fix tracked in #1804).
Log-persistence infrastructure for short-lived crashed pods (decision-8 D5: deferred to #1805; agent-diagnose ships against currently reachable evidence).

Fixing the in-situ gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL deployment misconfig (evidence-for-the-approach but out of scope; filed separately; validate_deployment_manifests should catch this class on re-encounter).
Replacing kubectl entirely. The 80% of debug flows that repeat every session are in scope; the long tail stays kubectl-shaped.
Sandbox-agent-facing tooling (#1765 is the flip-side concern for sandbox agents; not in #1759's scope).
Introducing a skills/operator/ vs skills/agent/ split (decision-8 D2: flat skills/ directory; re-evaluate when #1765 lands).
Multi-distro k8s support. decision-8 Q6 resolves k3s-only for day 1; GKE/EKS/AKS are explicit follow-ups.
Resolving overlap with the existing overseer agent (#1806 non-blocking investigation). Skills must reference #1806 but must not block on its outcome.

root_causes.title: MCP surface is pipeline-centric, not deployment-centric
root_causes.description: All 23 existing MCP tools (orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:64+) assume the orchestrator+gateway are already running and registered. The closest deployment-facing tool is check_health (schema at mcp_tools.py:276, handler at mcp_tools.py:1499) which only returns ok/not-ok. There is no tool that can answer 'what's actually running right now?', 'does my Kustomize manifest reference things that exist?', 'is Calico actually enforcing my NetworkPolicies?', or 'clean up stale worktrees from the previous deployment'.

root_causes.title: No runtime verification of the NetworkPolicy posture the k8s migration claims to enforce
root_causes.description: k8s/base/network-policies.yaml defines default-deny-ingress, default-deny-egress, allow-agent-to-gateway, allow-agent-to-orchestrator, allow-agent-dns. integration_tests/test_network_isolation.py (472 lines) and test_network_security.py (187 lines) probe egress but against the Docker-era network model. Nothing in the current test plan probes the actual Calico enforcement post-deploy, which is how #1769 (HITL resolve endpoint reachable from egg-agents) slipped through.

root_causes.title: Identifier-translation asymmetries are not surfaced as a first-class debugging concern
root_causes.description: The Pod-UID-vs-Job-UID translation lives at orchestrator/kubernetes_client.py:867-931 in _resolve_job_name. #1760 and #1764 were the same bug on two different surfaces (runtime reconciliation vs get_container_logs). A tool/skill that walks one container through every API surface on spawn would have surfaced both in one pass. The skill-layer pattern catalogue in agent-diagnose is the piece that makes this a solved class of bug instead of a recurring one.

root_causes.title: Worktree lifecycle spans two locations only one of which git tracks
root_causes.description: `git worktree prune` walks `.git/worktrees/` inside each repo but does NOT clean orphan directories under `~/.egg-worktrees/`, the shared worktree base managed by the gateway (gateway/worktree_manager.py:47 WORKTREE_BASE_DIR = /home/egg/.egg-worktrees). A stale worktree from a previous (Compose-era) run of egg broke the first pipeline submission on the new k3s deployment during the validation session. Cancelled pipelines later left orphan dirs that required manual `rm -rf`. The gateway already owns create_worktree (line 237), list_worktrees (line 1062), cleanup_orphaned_worktrees (line 1182) — a new prune_stale_worktrees MCP tool composes these and adds `git worktree prune` per-repo.

root_causes.title: Static validation of the Kustomize overlay against cluster state has no home
root_causes.description: Every deployment bug the validation session surfaced (invented /etc/egg-gateway/certs path, missing gateway-secrets Secret, /healthz vs /api/v1/health mismatch, auto-injected ORCHESTRATOR_PORT=tcp://…) was statically catchable against the applied manifest + cluster state. No tool today does that walk. The k8s/base/ Kustomize tree (namespaces.yaml, rbac.yaml, orchestrator-deployment.yaml, orchestrator-service.yaml, gateway-deployment.yaml, gateway-service.yaml, network-policies.yaml) is the canonical input; cluster state (Secrets, ConfigMaps, containerd image list, existing hostPaths) is the canonical comparand. validate_deployment_manifests is the tool that does this walk and warns on every mismatch.

root_causes.title: Recurring failure classes aren't codified as a pattern catalogue
root_causes.description: The validation session ran into the same failure shape three times in a row (#1760, #1764, #1766) before the human spotted the pattern. '403 from gateway: probably fine/coarse role mismatch', '404 on container ID: probably Pod UID vs Job UID mismatch', 'short-lived pod deleted before logs readable: persist out-of-band' — these are the judgment layer that makes agent-diagnose skill-shaped rather than tool-shaped. There is no place in the codebase today where such a catalogue lives.

mcp_surface_pattern.description: 23 MCP tools live as dicts in PIPELINE_TOOLS (orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:64-669) and as _handle_<tool> methods on class PipelineToolHandler (line 690+). Dispatch is via handle_tool_call (line 704) which maps tool name → handler. Each handler calls _make_request to proxy to an orchestrator HTTP route. The MCP server itself is an in-process FastMCP sidecar inside the orchestrator Deployment (orchestrator/mcp_server.py:1-60), rate-limited at 30 req/min (DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT at mcp_server.py:36), using streamable-HTTP transport. Adding a new tool is: (1) add schema to PIPELINE_TOOLS; (2) add _handle_<name> method on PipelineToolHandler; (3) wire into handle_tool_call's dispatch dict; (4) add orchestrator route under orchestrator/routes/ if new logic is needed; (5) add unit test that mocks _make_request(). Every one of the four new MCP tools follows this exact pattern.
files: orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1499 (check_health handler — illustrative of the proxy pattern)

skill_surface_pattern.description: Three skills today under skills/: sdlc/SKILL.md, babysit-pr/SKILL.md, egg-setup/SKILL.md. Each is a YAML-frontmatter markdown file with keys: name, description, disable-model-invocation (true), argument-hint. Filesystem-discovered — no registry file. No operator-vs-agent split (that's #1765's concern). New skills land as skills/deployment-diagnose/SKILL.md and skills/agent-diagnose/SKILL.md. Skill authoring guidance: the reviewer_agent_design review flagged that skills should be short orienting briefs — domain knowledge, evidence-chain hints, known-failure catalogue — NOT step-by-step procedures. agent-mode-design.md:295-303 names 'overloading with prescriptive checklists' as the anti-pattern to avoid. This is a plan-phase guardrail on the skill content, not on the scaffold.

kubernetes_client_layer.description: Official `kubernetes` python client, in-cluster auth via service account, singleton accessor get_kubernetes_client() (orchestrator/kubernetes_client.py:943). Shared by kubernetes_spawner.py (Job spawn + gateway session registration) and kubernetes_monitor.py (pod health, orphan cleanup). The Pod-UID-vs-Job-UID translation lives in _resolve_job_name() (line 867-931); this is exactly the surface #1760/#1764 reference. create_container creates a Job; create_job is at line 645. list_containers maps to pod.metadata.uid values and is the reason _resolve_job_name must handle Pod UIDs. New k8s-facing MCP tools reuse this singleton rather than re-establishing auth.

runtime_dispatch.description: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:390 reads EGG_RUNTIME env (default `docker`) and returns KubernetesSpawner or ContainerSpawner via _get_spawner(). Namespace defaults: orchestrator/gateway in egg-system, agent Jobs in egg-agents. The new k8s-specific tools (validate_deployment_manifests, validate_network_isolation, prune_stale_worktrees) must check EGG_RUNTIME and return a structured 'not available on this runtime' error when EGG_RUNTIME != 'kubernetes'. get_deployment_context is already designed to be multi-runtime — it reports whichever backend it finds.

kustomize_layout.description: k8s/base/ contains kustomization.yaml, namespaces.yaml (egg-system, egg-agents), rbac.yaml (egg-orchestrator ServiceAccount + ClusterRole + egg-agent-manager Role), orchestrator-deployment.yaml + orchestrator-service.yaml, gateway-deployment.yaml + gateway-service.yaml, network-policies.yaml (Calico). One local overlay at k8s/overlays/local/ with kustomization.yaml + patches/ for hostPath storage + local-path provisioner. This is the canonical input surface validate_deployment_manifests walks. Cross-reference: orchestrator-deployment.yaml:55 sets EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL; gateway-deployment.yaml does NOT — this is the in-situ bug the refiner surfaced and scoped out of #1759.

worktree_lifecycle.description: gateway/worktree_manager.py hardcodes WORKTREE_BASE_DIR = /home/egg/.egg-worktrees (line 47). Owns create_worktree (line 237), list_worktrees (line 1062), list_worktrees_for_pipeline (line 1120), cleanup_orphaned_worktrees (line 1182). The gateway pod mounts this path via hostPath. Both the gateway and the orchestrator know the path. prune_stale_worktrees composes cleanup_orphaned_worktrees with a per-repo `git worktree prune` sweep (which cleanup_orphaned_worktrees does NOT do).

existing_container_diagnosis_tools.description: list_containers (mcp_tools.py:284 schema) and get_container_logs (line 303 schema) already work against both Docker and k8s via the _get_monitor() dispatch in the orchestrator routes. agent-diagnose skill composes these rather than re-implementing them. The Pod-UID↔Job-name translation in _resolve_job_name() is what lets a caller pass back the container_id from list_containers to get_container_logs without knowing whether the runtime is Docker or k8s. send_message and get_consensus_status (mcp_tools.py:334, :365) are the other tools agent-diagnose composes to walk BRC state for a failed agent.

network_isolation_tests_today.description: integration_tests/test_network_isolation.py (472 lines) and integration_tests/test_network_security.py (187 lines) probe egress but against the Docker-era network model (egg-isolated 172.32.0.0/24, egg-external 172.33.0.0/24, fixed gateway IPs). Neither drives the k8s Calico NetworkPolicy enforcement path. validate_network_isolation is a runtime probe in egg-agents that verifies the claims in k8s/base/network-policies.yaml are actually being enforced by Calico. Decision 3 (feedback Q3) asks whether these tests should be migrated to drive validate_network_isolation or kept alongside — defer to reviewer_plan / human gate.

gateway_contract_api_env_misconfig.description: gateway/contract_api.py:72-73 reads EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL (default `http://egg-orchestrator:9849`, the Compose-era service name). The deployed k3s gateway Deployment does not set EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL, so the default resolves to a DNS name that does not exist in k8s (orchestrator-in-k8s is at orchestrator.egg-system.svc.cluster.local:9849). Every contract read/write from the sandbox fails with 'Orchestrator unreachable — try again'. This pipeline itself hit this bug during the refine phase; the architect-pipeline's egg-contract CLI is currently broken from the sandbox. The refiner correctly flagged this, correctly scoped the fix out of #1759, and correctly identified it as evidence-for-the-approach (validate_deployment_manifests is exactly the tool that catches this class). The plan phase should open a separate tracking issue for the env fix rather than smuggle it into #1759 — that will make the new tool's first acceptance test a real-world bug it catches.
files: k8s/base/orchestrator-deployment.yaml:55 (sets EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL — proof the pattern exists)

approaches_considered.name: Umbrella — ship 5 MCP tools + 2 skills in #1759 (refiner's recommended; D4 INCLUDE)
approaches_considered.description: One plan, one implement phase, all five MCP tools plus both skills land in a single PR. Existing patterns are reused throughout: new tool schemas added to PIPELINE_TOOLS, new handlers on PipelineToolHandler, new orchestrator routes under orchestrator/routes/, k8s work via get_kubernetes_client() singleton, skills added as new directories under skills/. Carve-outs (from decision-8): include rebuild_and_rollout now that #1763 has merged (D4); defer submit_task papercut to #1804 (D3); skills ship against currently reachable evidence with log-persistence tracked in #1805 (D5); file gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL fix as a separate issue.
pros: The issue is explicitly framed as a unified story — 'tools alone didn't help; skills close the validation loop'. Umbrella preserves that narrative in the PR description and commit log.

Acceptance criterion is testable end-to-end: re-run the #1692 validation pass using only the new tools/skills; does any step still require raw kubectl? This is the real success metric; splitting forfeits it.

Skills compose tools. Shipping the skills against unstable/nonexistent tools forces speculative writing or no-ops; shipping together means the skill reviewer can verify evidence chains against the actual tool outputs.
All four tools are small and independently testable (each has a bounded schema + a single route + a single handler). The skill work is also bounded — two SKILL.md files plus two docs pages.

The gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL bug encountered in this very pipeline is ready-made proof that validate_deployment_manifests is well-scoped. Landing the tool in the same PR that files the env-fix issue gives reviewers a concrete 'here's the bug it catches' data point.
cons: Larger diff than a split. Historical pattern at egg: large umbrella PRs occasionally stall in review. Mitigated because each of the six items has a small blast radius and the review graph (reviewer_code, reviewer_contract, tester-as-reviewer) already fans out across them.
One failed acceptance criterion can block the whole PR. Mitigated because no item is coupled to another at the commit level — any one can be reverted independently.
Requires the plan phase to enumerate acceptance criteria per item even though the PR is one unit. Not actually a cost — the task-planner is specifically for this.
approaches_considered.verdict: Recommended. This is the refiner's Option A with the refiner's four carve-outs. Nothing in the plan phase has surfaced a reason to diverge.

approaches_considered.name: Split by shape — tools first, skills in a follow-up issue
approaches_considered.description: Ship the four MCP tools in #1759's PR; open a follow-up issue for the two skills once the tools land. The skills then compose stable primitives instead of moving targets.
pros: Smaller reviews, less coupling between reviewers.
Skills can be authored after real-world tool use has validated their shape — reduces the risk a skill prescribes an evidence chain the tools can't supply.
cons: Forfeits the end-to-end acceptance criterion ('re-run #1692 validation using only the new surface'). The whole point of the issue is that tools alone didn't help; skills are the judgment layer. Splitting defers the thing the issue actually argues for.
Two issues to track → two refine/plan cycles → higher coordination cost.
Skills-follow-up sits exposed as 'future work' with no owner; historical pattern is that such follow-ups slip.
approaches_considered.verdict: Rejected — forfeits the acceptance criterion the issue was written around.

approaches_considered.name: Split per-item — open child issues for each tool and each skill
approaches_considered.description: Close #1759 as a tracker; open one issue per MCP tool and per skill (6 issues total). Each child goes through its own full SDLC pipeline.
cons: Enormous coordination overhead — 6 pipelines for 6 small deliverables, each with its own refine/plan/implement BRC cycle.
Both skills overlap heavily in evidence-gathering primitives (pod describe, Events, logs, env). Splitting them duplicates design work and yields inconsistent output formats.
Loses the unified validation-retrospective framing that makes the issue a story rather than a shopping list.
approaches_considered.verdict: Rejected — coordination overhead is disproportionate to item size.

approaches_considered.name: Tools now, skills blocked on log persistence
approaches_considered.description: Ship the four MCP tools in #1759. Defer both skills until log-persistence (preserve failed pods / stream agent logs out-of-band) lands, on the grounds that agent-diagnose is significantly less useful without reachable logs for <10s-lived pods.
pros: Avoids shipping agent-diagnose as a half-measure against its own motivating failure mode.
Forces log persistence to be resolved explicitly.
cons: deployment-diagnose does NOT depend on log persistence — holding it back is conservative in the wrong direction.
agent-diagnose is still useful for the majority of failures (pods that don't die in <10s). Waiting delays shipping value that already exists.
Log persistence is an orthogonal infrastructure change that doesn't belong inside #1759's tooling-gap story.
approaches_considered.verdict: Rejected — log persistence is a separately-tracked concern; see Decision 5.

recommended_approach.name: Approach A — umbrella ship of 5 MCP tools + 2 skills, per decision-8 resolution
recommended_approach.justification: Approach A is the only option that preserves the issue's core acceptance criterion (re-run the #1692 validation session using only new tools/skills without falling back to raw kubectl or raw `make redeploy`). Every other option forfeits that criterion or sequences the skills work behind tool shape validation that doesn't actually need to happen. decision-8 resolves all carve-outs: rebuild_and_rollout is INCLUDED (D4, since #1763 merged); submit_task papercut deferred to #1804 (D3); log persistence deferred to #1805 (D5); the gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL bug is separately filable evidence. The patterns to reuse are explicit: schemas in PIPELINE_TOOLS, handlers on PipelineToolHandler, orchestrator routes under orchestrator/routes/ for new HTTP surfaces, k8s work via get_kubernetes_client(), skills as SKILL.md files under skills/ following the existing sdlc/babysit-pr/egg-setup frontmatter pattern. Auth: lifecycle-secret required on mutating routes (tool_2 probe, tool_3 dry_run=False, tool_5 rebuild); read-only tools stay on session auth. No new architecture. No new review-graph shape.

tool_1_validate_deployment_manifests.description: Dry-run validation against the current Kustomize overlay + cluster state. Input: optional overlay path (default k8s/overlays/local/). Output: a list of findings with severity (warn/error) and location. Warning rules from the issue: (1) Secret/ConfigMap references missing in cluster; (2) hostPath mounts whose host path doesn't exist on the gateway node; (3) imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent with a tag not present in k3s containerd; (4) Deployment whose Service selector labels don't match its pod template; (5) service-env-var collisions with user-set env vars (GATEWAY_PORT, ORCHESTRATOR_PORT); (6) env-var presence check — e.g. gateway Deployment missing EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL. Implementation: new route POST /api/v1/cluster/validate-manifests under a new orchestrator/routes/cluster.py module. Handler runs `kubectl kustomize <overlay> | yaml.safe_load_all` and cross-references with the kubernetes client (list Secrets, ConfigMaps, check containerd image list via `k3s ctr images ls` or the kubelet images API). Returns structured findings. MCP schema mirrors the existing validate_config (mcp_tools.py:526) shape — a thin input dict and a findings array output. Runtime gating (risk_analyst RISK-5): the tool must first read EGG_RUNTIME; if != 'kubernetes' it returns a runtime_unsupported error. k3s-specific checks (#3 containerd image list, and the local-path-provisioner hostPath checks) must be further gated on get_deployment_context reporting a k3s cluster — on a non-k3s cluster these checks emit UNVERIFIED rather than a false error. Mixed-distro guardrail so the tool is safe to run on any k8s eventually without returning misleading findings.
files: orchestrator/mcp_tools.py (PIPELINE_TOOLS: new schema entry; _handle_validate_deployment_manifests; dispatch wiring)
orchestrator/kubernetes_client.py (may extend with list_secrets/list_configmaps if not already present)

tool_2_validate_network_isolation.description: Spawn a throwaway probe Job in egg-agents and verify the four claims from the issue: (1) can reach gateway Service; (2) cannot reach internet directly (curl https://google.com + DNS lookup for random domains); (3) cannot reach other agent pods; (4) cannot reach orchestrator directly (only via gateway session). Input: optional pipeline_id + role (to tag the probe Job accordingly). Output: a pass/fail result per claim plus raw probe output. Implementation: new route POST /api/v1/cluster/validate-network-isolation under orchestrator/routes/cluster.py. Handler first calls get_deployment_context (or inlines the same check) and probes for an enforcing CNI (DaemonSet calico-node in kube-system, or equivalent); if NetworkPolicy enforcement is NOT detected, the handler returns a single CNI_NOT_ENFORCING diagnostic and refuses to spawn the probe so no false-positive passes are emitted (risk_analyst RISK-5, DEP-3). Otherwise handler uses kubernetes_client to create a short-lived Job with image per decision-8 D6 (reuse sandbox image and run curl+DNS probes). Probe Job pod template MUST set labels `app.kubernetes.io/component: agent` + `egg.probe: true` so it falls under exactly the same NetworkPolicy allow/deny rules a real agent does (risk_analyst RISK-1). The `egg.probe: true` label lets NetworkPolicy selectors in real pipelines explicitly exclude probes without risk of overlap. Env must be built from an empty base and NEVER inherit orchestrator env — reuse kubernetes_spawner's _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS denylist to guarantee no lifecycle secrets leak to any egress target (risk_analyst RISK-1). Job spec: backoffLimit=0, activeDeadlineSeconds=30 (tight per RISK-1), ttlSecondsAfterFinished=0 so the Job GCs immediately after completion. Route requires lifecycle-secret auth (mutating; risk_analyst RISK-4). Because Job scheduling + run + cleanup can exceed FastMCP's ~60s request timeout (risk_analyst RISK-8), the MCP tool uses a two-call pattern: the first call returns a probe_id and starts the Job; the second call fetches results by probe_id once the Job has reported. Job name uses probe-<timestamp>-<short-uuid>. Tests (integration) must include a kind/minikube+Calico run where the probe Job is diffed against a real agent pod spec: identical NetworkPolicy selection, identical protected-env handling.
files: orchestrator/kubernetes_client.py (may add a spawn_probe_job helper if the existing create_job isn't reusable enough)
integration_tests/test_k8s_network_isolation.py (new — drives the MCP tool against a real Calico cluster; replaces or complements existing Docker-era tests)

tool_3_prune_stale_worktrees.description: Clean up across both worktree locations and report what got removed: (1) `git worktree prune` inside each configured repo's .git/worktrees/; (2) orphan directories under WORKTREE_BASE_DIR (/home/egg/.egg-worktrees) that do not correspond to an active pipeline — cleanup_orphaned_worktrees at gateway/worktree_manager.py:1182 already covers most of this but does not do the per-repo git prune. Input: optional repo filter, dry_run (default True). Output: structured list of what was removed + per-location stats. Ownership (decision-8 D7): the MCP tool itself is orchestrator-owned (schema in PIPELINE_TOOLS, handler on PipelineToolHandler, route POST /api/v1/cluster/prune-worktrees under orchestrator/routes/cluster.py) — matches the pattern of every other MCP tool. The filesystem mutation and the worktree mutex live in the gateway (gateway/worktree_manager.py holds WORKTREE_BASE_DIR and cleanup_orphaned_worktrees, and only the gateway pod has the hostPath mount). So the orchestrator route proxies to a NEW gateway endpoint (e.g. POST /internal/worktrees/prune under gateway/worktree_api.py or gateway/routes/worktrees.py) that owns the actual `git worktree prune` + orphan-dir sweep under the existing worktree mutex (risk_analyst RISK-2). The proxy is internal-only (egg-system-scoped; ClusterIP Service), and the orchestrator authenticates to the gateway using the existing inter-service mechanism — no new auth surface. dry_run=True is the safe default; dry_run=False is explicit and logs a loud audit record via the orchestrator's existing logging stack. decision-8 Q7 resolved: dry_run is a sufficient gate for the local-dev persona; no second confirmation flag is required. Destructive-by-design, always.
files: gateway/routes/worktrees.py or gateway/worktree_api.py (new — exposes prune endpoint to orchestrator)
gateway/worktree_manager.py (extend cleanup_orphaned_worktrees with a per-repo git-prune sweep; make dry_run first-class)

tool_4_get_deployment_context.description: Return where egg is actually running right now. Multi-runtime by design. Output fields: runtime (docker|kubernetes), kubeconfig_context + cluster_info (k8s only), namespace (egg-system), cni + network_policy_enforcement_status (probes for Calico presence via `kubectl get daemonset calico-node -n kube-system`), and image_tag per control-plane component (orchestrator, gateway) with source (manifest vs running pod). With #1763 merged, image_tag carries SHA-tagged provenance (manifest-tag == running-imageID when correctly rolled out). Implementation: new route GET /api/v1/cluster/deployment-context under orchestrator/routes/cluster.py. Handler reads EGG_RUNTIME, dispatches to a k8s path (uses get_kubernetes_client to describe the orchestrator/gateway Deployments and Pods, extract image + imageID; checks for Calico DaemonSet in kube-system) or a Docker path (uses docker_client.list_containers, extracts image tag). Both paths return the same output shape. No inputs. This tool is the central runtime-classifier that tool_1, tool_2, and tool_5 call first to gate their k3s-specific behavior (risk_analyst RISK-5).
files: orchestrator/docker_client.py (may add analogous helper for the docker-runtime path)

tool_5_rebuild_and_rollout.description: Thin MCP wrapper over `make redeploy` so operators can trigger a full local-dev rebuild+rollout from inside the MCP surface without dropping to a shell. decision-8 D4 resolved INCLUDE IN SCOPE because #1763 (SHA-tagged local images) has merged — image provenance is now deterministic enough for this flow to be trustworthy. Input: optional components filter (default: orchestrator + gateway), optional wait_for_ready bool (default True), optional timeout_seconds (default 600). Output: {progress_id: str, started: true} on the async start path; the operator polls a progress endpoint for streaming status (build → import to k3s containerd → kubectl apply → rollout status → readiness probe). Implementation: new route POST /api/v1/cluster/rebuild-and-rollout under orchestrator/routes/cluster.py. Handler spawns the rebuild in a background task (re-using the orchestrator's existing progress API under orchestrator/routes/progress.py) and returns a progress_id immediately — it does NOT block on the rebuild. Streaming (risk_analyst RISK-8): build + k3s-containerd image-import + kubectl rollout can exceed FastMCP's ~60s request timeout, so the MCP tool returns quickly and the caller follows up via get_progress (existing MCP tool) or a new poll call, matching the two-call pattern used by other long-running orchestrator operations. Auth: lifecycle-secret REQUIRED (mutating operation; rebuild shells out to `make redeploy` which writes to containerd and the live cluster — risk_analyst RISK-4). Runtime gating (RISK-5): must read EGG_RUNTIME; on EGG_RUNTIME=docker the tool returns a runtime_unsupported error recommending `make redeploy` directly. Implementation choice: handler invokes `make redeploy` via subprocess with cwd=repo root, streams stdout/stderr to the progress API, and captures the final kubectl rollout status as structured output. The Makefile is authoritative; the tool does not duplicate the shell steps. Acceptance: operator kicks off a rebuild from the skill/MCP session, observes progress streaming, sees the new orchestrator+gateway running (imageID matches expected SHA), all without dropping to a shell. Non-blocking MCP means the skill can continue other work while the rebuild runs. Must not be called from within a pipeline (the orchestrator it would rebuild is the one serving the pipeline); the handler rejects calls that originate from sandbox-scoped sessions — lifecycle-secret alone is sufficient enforcement for the local-dev persona.
files: orchestrator/mcp_tools.py (schema + handler + dispatch; input: components/wait/timeout; output: progress_id)
orchestrator/routes/progress.py (reused — tracks build+import+rollout steps; may extend with well-known step keys for this flow)
orchestrator/background.py or similar (queue the rebuild task; orchestrator already has a pattern for background jobs — confirm with implement-phase code-reading)
Makefile (confirm `make redeploy` target covers build + k3s import + rollout as currently practiced; no new target unless the existing one lacks a piece)
integration_tests/test_rebuild_and_rollout.py (new — opt-in; spawns a real k3s cluster, runs the tool end-to-end, asserts imageID changes)

skill_1_deployment_diagnose.description: New skill at skills/deployment-diagnose/SKILL.md. Frontmatter: name: deployment-diagnose, description: 'Diagnose the egg control plane on a fresh deployment. Walks pod status, Events, image-vs-manifest drift, resolved mounts, health-endpoint bodies, applied-vs-running spec drift, and silent-failure log bursts; produces a prioritized human-readable report.', disable-model-invocation: true, argument-hint: '[--namespace egg-system] [--since <duration>]'. Body is a short orienting brief per reviewer_agent_design's guidance: domain knowledge (what to look at, in what order, for which failure modes), an evidence-chain hint sheet (pod phase → container statuses → Events → image-ID vs manifest → mounted Secrets/ConfigMaps → health endpoint body → applied-vs-running spec diff → gateway + orchestrator silent-failure scan). Silent-failure scan shape (decision-8 Q4): scan BOTH gateway and orchestrator pod logs; signature-match via structured-fields first with hash-of-stripped-line fallback; burst threshold 3+ in any 60s window; last ~2000 lines; human-invoked only (not continuous). Known-failure catalogue: 272-consecutive-checkpoint-fail-burst from #1767; :latest-tag-unchanged-so-rollout-skipped from #1692; Secret-reference-doesn't-exist from the validation session; service-env-var collisions like ORCHESTRATOR_PORT=tcp://…; gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL missing. Composes: check_health, list_containers, get_container_logs, validate_deployment_manifests, get_deployment_context. Explicit reference to #1806 (overseer-overlap investigation, non-blocking): this skill and the existing overseer agent both detect control-plane anomalies; the SKILL.md body must link #1806 and note the intended split (overseer = continuous, deployment-diagnose = human-invoked deep-walk) so the two are built in coordination rather than in isolation (risk_analyst RISK-11). Authoring guardrail (agent-mode-design.md:295-303): do NOT write a step-by-step procedure; write what to look at and why.
files: docs/guides/deployment-diagnose.md (new — deeper reference doc; SKILL.md links here; links to #1806)
docs/index.md (add new guide to the index)

skill_2_agent_diagnose.description: New skill at skills/agent-diagnose/SKILL.md. Frontmatter: name: agent-diagnose, description: 'Diagnose why a spawned agent pod failed. Walks the Job spec, Pod status, last 100 lines of logs, Events, resolved env, and synthetic gateway egress probe; pattern-matches symptoms to known failure classes.', disable-model-invocation: true, argument-hint: '<pipeline-id> <agent-role>'. Body includes a pattern-matched-failure catalogue as the core value-add: '403 from gateway → probably fine/coarse role mismatch (see #1766 pattern); 404 on container ID → probably Pod UID vs Job UID (see #1760/#1764); short-lived pod deleted before logs readable → persist out-of-band (#1805); OOMKill exit → bump memory in Job spec; ImagePull failure → k3s ctr images import or :latest tag unchanged (less common since #1763); NetworkPolicy denial silent → run validate_network_isolation to confirm egress posture'. Identifier-translation asymmetries catalogue (decision-8 Q2, verbatim): (a) Pod UID ↔ Job UID (#1760, #1764); (b) session token ↔ container_id; (c) issue number ↔ pipeline_id ↔ branch name (#1773); (d) task_id ↔ agent role ↔ container name; (e) contract field path `decisions.N` vs bare `decisions` (#1801 analysis). The catalogue entry explicitly names each asymmetry as a failure-class pattern with a canonical example and the tool that resolves the shape (typically _resolve_job_name at orchestrator/kubernetes_client.py:867-931 or the contract field-path normalizer). Composed primitives: list_containers, get_container_logs (pod-level evidence); validate_network_isolation (synthetic egress probe — replaces the earlier draft which incorrectly named get_consensus_status/send_message here; those are pipeline-state tools, not network probes); get_deployment_context (runtime classification); get_consensus_status + send_message are still allowed if the skill needs to cross-check BRC state for the failed agent, but they do NOT act as the egress probe. Constraint from decision-8 D5: ships against currently reachable evidence; log persistence for <10s-lived pods tracked in #1805. Explicit reference to #1806 (overseer overlap): SKILL.md body must link #1806 and note that the pattern catalogue is the deliberate skill-layer companion to the overseer's continuous-monitoring role (risk_analyst RISK-11). Same authoring guardrail as deployment-diagnose.

docs/guides/agent-diagnose.md (new — deeper reference; links to #1806 and to _resolve_job_name)

mcp_rate_limit_consideration.description: The MCP server is rate-limited at 30 req/min (orchestrator/mcp_server.py:36). deployment-diagnose fires several tool calls in sequence (probably 5-8); agent-diagnose similar. At 30 rpm, a single skill invocation is well within budget. Skill-level recursion risk (explicit guardrail): agent-diagnose invoked on a failed agent MUST NOT re-invoke agent-diagnose on every pod it examines in its catalogue walk — that loops at k*pods_per_namespace requests and will hit 30 rpm quickly on a busy cluster. Similarly, deployment-diagnose calling agent-diagnose on every agent Job it finds would recurse. Constraint: each skill walks a bounded set of evidence per invocation and emits a textual 'consider running agent-diagnose on <agent>' recommendation rather than auto-expanding. reviewer_agent_design flagged this explicitly as a plan-phase question. Recommended: document the budget, keep the default at 30 rpm, and if practice shows the limit is hit, bump it per-role rather than have the skill self-throttle. Not a code change in this issue — a plan-phase note for the authoring agent and a docs mention in the SKILL.md body that explicitly prohibits recursive skill invocation.

runtime_fallback_behavior.description: The four k8s-specific tools (validate_deployment_manifests, validate_network_isolation, prune_stale_worktrees, rebuild_and_rollout) must handle EGG_RUNTIME=docker gracefully. The recommended shape (matching how list_containers/get_container_logs already work): the handler returns a structured error with `error_code='runtime_unsupported'` and a human message 'This tool requires EGG_RUNTIME=kubernetes; current runtime is docker.'. The MCP tool schema documents the requirement. get_deployment_context is the only tool that runs on both — same output shape, different population logic. Additionally (risk_analyst RISK-5), k3s-specific heuristics INSIDE each tool (e.g. tool_1's `k3s ctr images ls` check, tool_5's `make redeploy` which uses k3s ctr import) must be gated on get_deployment_context reporting a k3s cluster; on a non-k3s k8s flavor they emit UNVERIFIED rather than misleading findings.

probe_pod_design_resolved_d6.description: decision-8 D6 resolved: reuse the sandbox image and run curl/DNS probes from a short-lived Job; delete the Job after results are collected. Rationale: one image to maintain, already trusted by the gateway, network tools (curl, nslookup) already present. Risk-analyst RISK-1 mitigations layered on top: explicit labels (app.kubernetes.io/component: agent + egg.probe: true), _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS denylist when constructing probe env, activeDeadlineSeconds=30, ttlSecondsAfterFinished=0.

skill_directory_resolved_d2.description: decision-8 D2 resolved: flat skills/ — add deployment-diagnose and agent-diagnose alongside existing sdlc/babysit-pr/egg-setup. Rationale: existing convention, no harness change, low friction. If #1765 (agent-facing tool discoverability for sandbox agents) introduces a split later, a rename is a mechanical follow-up.

tool_placement_resolved_d7.description: decision-8 D7 resolved: orchestrator-owned routes + gateway proxying only where necessary. All five MCP tools live in orchestrator/mcp_tools.py with routes under orchestrator/routes/cluster.py. Tool_3 prune_stale_worktrees is the only tool that reaches into gateway-owned state (WORKTREE_BASE_DIR + worktree mutex); the orchestrator route proxies to a new gateway endpoint (e.g. POST /internal/worktrees/prune under gateway/worktree_api.py or gateway/routes/worktrees.py) that owns the actual filesystem mutation. Tool_2 validate_network_isolation spawns a Job, which is orchestrator-territory. Tool_1, tool_4, tool_5 are pure orchestrator-side. This matches the pattern of every existing MCP tool.

acceptance_criteria_matrix.description: End-to-end acceptance criterion from the issue: a replay of the #1692 validation session using only the new tools/skills does not fall back to raw kubectl (or raw `make redeploy`) for any of the documented failure modes. Per-item criteria below.

items.criterion: Catches the gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL missing-env bug surfaced in this pipeline as a warn-level finding.
Catches a Secret reference that doesn't exist in the cluster (reproduce by referencing gateway-secrets before creating it).
Catches a hostPath whose host path doesn't exist on the node (reproduce with /etc/egg-gateway/certs).
On EGG_RUNTIME != kubernetes returns runtime_unsupported rather than crashing. k3s-specific rules emit UNVERIFIED on a non-k3s flavor.

Probe succeeds against the gateway Service; fails against internet; fails against other agent pods; fails against orchestrator-direct. Captures #1769 class: any endpoint that shouldn't be reachable from egg-agents shows up.
When CNI enforcement is not detected (DaemonSet absent / different CNI without NetworkPolicy support) the tool returns CNI_NOT_ENFORCING and refuses to run the probe.

Probe Job carries labels app.kubernetes.io/component=agent AND egg.probe=true; NetworkPolicy treats it identically to a real agent; env is built from empty base with _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS denylist; Job self-deletes via ttlSecondsAfterFinished=0 + activeDeadlineSeconds=30.
dry_run=True reports the orphan-dir case that broke the first k3s pipeline submission without mutating state.
dry_run=False actually removes the orphan and logs an audit entry; the orchestrator route proxies to a new gateway endpoint that owns the worktree mutex and filesystem access.
Reports runtime=kubernetes + current imageID vs manifest image-tag; surfaces image-drift or :latest-unchanged-so-rollout-skipped case; reports CNI enforcement status for tool_2 to consume.

MCP call returns progress_id within 5s without blocking; progress API streams build/import/rollout steps; final imageID on the running pods matches the newly-built SHA-tagged image (post #1763); lifecycle-secret required; runtime_unsupported on EGG_RUNTIME=docker.
A failed build (e.g. pinned syntax error) surfaces as a structured error on the progress stream rather than a hung MCP call or silent success.

Invoked on a broken control plane, produces a prioritized report that names the failure class (missing Secret / silent-failure burst / image-drift) and points at the piece of evidence that makes it obvious, not a dump. Scans BOTH gateway and orchestrator logs (decision-8 Q4).

Invoked on a failed agent Job, produces a report that names the failure class from the catalogue (Pod UID vs Job UID / role mismatch / OOMKill / ImagePull / NetworkPolicy denial) and enumerates the five identifier-translation asymmetries from decision-8 Q2 as first-class debugging hints.
SKILL.md bodies explicitly reference #1806 so overseer-overlap is visible to reviewers and future maintainers.

A human runs the #1692 validation session with only these new MCP tools + skills available and does not reach for raw kubectl or raw `make redeploy` for any of #1760, #1764, #1766, #1767, #1768, #1769.

dependencies_and_constraints.no_new_auth_surface_for_read_tools: The four read-mostly MCP tools (validate_deployment_manifests, validate_network_isolation, prune_stale_worktrees with dry_run=True, get_deployment_context) run inside the orchestrator's existing MCP server (orchestrator/mcp_server.py). The authenticated path is already the MCP request. Tools that reach into the cluster use the existing in-cluster ServiceAccount via get_kubernetes_client().
dependencies_and_constraints.lifecycle_secret_required_for_mutating_t: Mutating tools MUST require lifecycle-secret auth (risk_analyst RISK-4): validate_network_isolation (spawns a Job), prune_stale_worktrees with dry_run=False (mutates hostPath), rebuild_and_rollout (rebuilds images and replaces running pods). Plan-phase deliverable: an explicit per-route auth table in the task-planner output so code review can cross-check the decorators (risk_analyst Action Item). Read-only calls with dry_run=True or tool_1/tool_4 stay on session auth.
dependencies_and_constraints.dual_runtime_compatibility: The orchestrator still needs to run against Docker for local dev (EGG_RUNTIME=docker). Four of the five new tools are k8s-specific and must return a structured 'not available on this runtime' error. get_deployment_context is multi-runtime by design. k3s-specific heuristics inside tools are further gated on get_deployment_context reporting a k3s cluster (risk_analyst RISK-5).
dependencies_and_constraints.mcp_rate_limit: 30 req/min (orchestrator/mcp_server.py:36 DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT). A single skill invocation (5-8 tool calls) fits within budget; recursive invocation does not. SKILL.md bodies must explicitly prohibit skill-to-skill or self recursion for catalogue walks. Plan-phase note, not a code change.
dependencies_and_constraints.mcp_request_timeout_two_call_pattern: FastMCP Streamable HTTP has a ~60s per-request timeout (risk_analyst RISK-8). validate_network_isolation (probe schedule + run + cleanup) and rebuild_and_rollout (build + import + rollout) can exceed this. Both tools use a two-call pattern: the first call returns an id (probe_id / progress_id) and starts async work; the second call (or get_progress for rebuild) fetches results. Avoids orphaned Jobs or dangling builds on timeout.
dependencies_and_constraints.probe_pod_side_effects: validate_network_isolation spawns a probe Job in egg-agents. Job labels: app.kubernetes.io/component: agent + egg.probe: true (risk_analyst RISK-1). Env built from empty base with _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS denylist. Job spec: activeDeadlineSeconds=30, ttlSecondsAfterFinished=0, backoffLimit=0. NetworkPolicy must treat it identically to a real agent pod.
dependencies_and_constraints.cni_enforcement_prerequisite: NetworkPolicy evaluation requires an enforcing CNI (Calico on k3s by default). If absent, validate_network_isolation returns CNI_NOT_ENFORCING and refuses to run the probe (risk_analyst RISK-5, DEP-3). This is exactly the 'false pass' failure mode: probe succeeds trivially on a non-enforcing CNI and misleadingly reports 'isolation verified'.
dependencies_and_constraints.host_filesystem_writes: prune_stale_worktrees(dry_run=false) mutates hostPath state on the gateway node. dry_run=True is the safe default; audit-log all destructive operations. decision-8 Q7 resolved: dry_run alone is a sufficient gate for the local-dev persona; no second confirmation flag.
dependencies_and_constraints.skill_authoring_guardrail: reviewer_agent_design's non-blocking note: skills should be short orienting briefs (domain knowledge, evidence-chain hints, known-failure catalogue), NOT step-by-step procedures. agent-mode-design.md:295-303 names 'overloading with prescriptive checklists' as the anti-pattern. Task-planner should make this explicit in the skill-authoring task.
dependencies_and_constraints.blocked_on_other_work: Nothing in #1759's scope is blocked. #1763 (SHA-tagged local images) has merged, unblocking rebuild_and_rollout (decision-8 D4). #1804 (submit_task papercut), #1805 (log persistence), #1806 (overseer-overlap investigation) are all separate, non-blocking follow-ups tracked in the contract.
dependencies_and_constraints.decoupled_from_in_situ_bug: gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL misconfig in k8s/base/gateway-deployment.yaml is evidence-for-the-approach but OUT OF SCOPE for #1759. Plan/implement phase should file this as a new issue and validate_deployment_manifests's first real-world catch.
dependencies_and_constraints.related_issue_cluster: The plan should explicitly note which of the following issues the new skills assume are separately tracked: #1760 (Pod-UID vs Job-UID runtime reconciliation false-positive), #1764 (same bug on get_container_logs surface), #1765 (agent-facing tool discoverability — the flip side), #1766 (fine-coarse role mapping), #1767 (silent checkpoint failures), #1768 (feedback field-owner default), #1769 (HITL resolve endpoint auth), #1773 (issue-number↔pipeline_id↔branch-name identifier work), #1801 (contract field-path analysis), #1804 (submit_task papercut), #1805 (log persistence for short-lived pods), #1806 (overseer overlap investigation), #1763 (SHA-tag local images — MERGED).
dependencies_and_constraints.write_boundaries_gateway_enforced: The implementer role is scoped to {orchestrator/, sandbox/, gateway/, k8s/, docs/, tests/, integration_tests/, skills/, Makefile}. No part of the recommended design crosses that boundary.
dependencies_and_constraints.egg_contract_cli_broken_in_this_pipeline: reviewer_refine noted that egg-contract CLI from the sandbox is currently broken (gateway EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL bug). HITL decisions and feedback were registered by direct API call. Task-planner should treat the contract store as authoritative even if `egg-contract show` errors locally.

open_questions.question: Should validate_deployment_manifests default to overlay=k8s/overlays/local/ or require explicit overlay selection?
options: Default to k8s/overlays/local/ (matches make deploy; matches decision-8 Q1 local-dev persona)
Require explicit — fail if no overlay is selected
open_questions.notes: Default is easier; explicit is safer in multi-overlay environments. Probably default-with-override once more overlays exist (GKE follow-up — not day 1 per decision-8 Q6).

open_questions.question: Should validate_network_isolation's probe Job be owned by egg-agents or a new egg-probes namespace?
options: Reuse egg-agents (matches the policy surface being probed — risk_analyst RISK-1 accepts this given label gating egg.probe: true)
New egg-probes namespace with its own NetworkPolicy posture
open_questions.notes: Reusing egg-agents is the point — probing from a namespace with a different policy wouldn't validate the actual claim. Separate namespace adds a deploy step; defer unless probe-vs-real-agent collision becomes a real problem. risk_analyst's RISK-1 mitigations (explicit labels + _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS denylist) make the egg-agents option safe.
